heroPoints: Clinic review prompts work best when they respect patient flow and do not interrupt the service experience.
Acrylic review cards, countertop prompts and stickers each fit different reception and checkout setups.
The first pilot should test staff handoff, patient phone behavior and the actual review completion moment together.

faq.question: Where do clinic review cards usually work best?
faq.answer: They usually work best at a calm checkout or reception moment where staff can naturally invite feedback without slowing patient flow or interrupting care.

faq.question: Should clinics use a card or sticker first?
faq.answer: That depends on the reception workflow. A delivered card often works better in guided interactions, while a sticker can fit a stable desk prompt when staff involvement is lighter.
